summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by gastrostomy tube dependence and post-surgical malabsorption presented with worsening severe pain at the G-tube site without fever, chills, or visible change at the site. Given recent similar admission with CT showing inflammatory changes around the tube but no abscess or hematoma, she was evaluated by the bariatric surgery team; a trial of steroid administration through the G-tube provided minimal relief, so she was admitted for symptom control and nutrition management. Pain control improved after transitioning from oral oxycodone to oral hydromorphone. A trial of bolus tube feeds led to hypoglycemia after boluses, so she was returned to continuous tube feeds and discharged home hemodynamically stable, ambulatory, and tolerating the regimen, with instructions to continue glucose monitoring, resume home medications, and follow up with her surgeon.
